_metadata.linear_workspace_inference_source: Inferred from .github/pull_request_template.md line 7, which links to https://linear.app/rudderstack/search. The Linear workspace slug in linear.app URLs is the path segment immediately after the host; here that segment is 'rudderstack'. This is the upstream RudderStack project's Linear workspace, inherited via the PR template. The actual workspace used by the Blitzy-Sandbox/blitzy-RudderStack fork (if any) cannot be confirmed without API access, because the PR template is text-only and the Linear API key is required to enumerate workspace membership programmatically.
_metadata.artifact_kind_note: This is a hand-authored seed artifact produced for the no-network-access analysis sandbox. The issues[] and labels_catalog[] arrays are intentionally empty because scripts/08_extract_linear.py cannot reach https://api.linear.app/graphql from the read-only sandbox: the LINEAR_API_KEY environment variable is not set, and the Linear GraphQL API requires an authenticated bearer token for every query (the API rejects all unauthenticated requests). When the script is re-run with LINEAR_API_KEY set and network reachable, it overwrites this file with the populated issue inventory and label catalogue; the run_id and extraction_timestamp will then reflect that execution. The linear.* sub-object below documents the GraphQL queries that would be issued so that the Reproducibility Appendix in acceleration-report.md is complete even when the API is unavailable.

linear.unavailable_reason: LINEAR_API_KEY environment variable is not set
linear.unavailable_reason_detail: The read-only analysis sandbox does not have a Linear API key configured. Per AAP §0.1.5 and §0.2.4 (Metric 12 row), Linear API access is conditional on the LINEAR_API_KEY environment variable being supplied. When the key is absent, scripts/08_extract_linear.py exits early with a structured 'unavailable' log line (per AAP §0.5.6 Observability discipline) and persists this seed artifact unchanged. No HTTP request is attempted; no PII or secret material is read from disk.
linear.auth_required: LINEAR_API_KEY environment variable (Linear personal API key or OAuth token with read scope on the workspace).
linear.consequence: Without Linear API access, metrics.json#m6 (Flow Distribution) cannot use Linear issue labels as the primary classifier. Per AAP §0.2.4 row m6, the classifier degrades to tier 2 (conventional-commit prefix on PR title via .github/workflows/semantic-pr.yaml allowed list) and tier 3 (keyword match on PR title/body). Confidence on m6 may drop to 'medium' (or 'low' if the unknown rate exceeds 20% in either phase). Similarly, metrics.json#m12 (Defects Out of SLA) cannot retrieve defect-labelled issues or slaBreachedAt/slaTargetDuration fields from Linear; combined with the absence of a SLA policy document in the repo (see slas.json), m12 must report 'insufficient_signal' per AAP §0.5.3.13.
graphql_queries_template: query Issues($filter: IssueFilter, $first: Int, $after: String) { issues(filter: $filter, first: $first, after: $after) { pageInfo { hasNextPage endCursor } nodes { id identifier title state { name } priority labels { nodes { name } } createdAt completedAt slaBreachedAt slaTargetDuration } } }
query Labels { issueLabels { nodes { id name color description } } }
linear.graphql_queries_template_note: These two queries are the exact strings that scripts/08_extract_linear.py would POST to https://api.linear.app/graphql when LINEAR_API_KEY is set. The Issues query paginates via Relay-style cursors (pageInfo.hasNextPage, pageInfo.endCursor) and filters by created_at >= analysis_period_start. The Labels query enumerates the full IssueLabel inventory once per run (no pagination needed for typical workspace sizes). Both queries are recorded verbatim here so that a future analyst with API access can paste them directly into the Linear GraphQL playground at https://studio.apollographql.com/public/Linear-API/variant/current/explorer to reproduce the extraction step. The queries are also referenced from the Reproducibility Appendix of acceleration-report.md.

filters_intended.since_date_note: Lower bound matches analysis_period_start (the Monday on or after the earliest commit on main, per AAP §0.5.6 window mechanics). Issues created before this date are excluded because they cannot be attributed to the baseline or post-introduction phases of THIS repository's analysis.
filters_intended.until_date_note: Upper bound matches analysis_period_end (one second before the Monday following the latest commit on main).

summary.summary_note: All counts are zero because no Linear API access was available at extraction time. When LINEAR_API_KEY is supplied and the script is re-run, these counters will be re-derived from the populated issues[] array using the label_categories_mapping defined in linear.filters_intended.label_categories_mapping. The label_distribution_by_phase sub-object groups the per-category counts by 'baseline' (issues with created_at < inflection_date_utc) and 'post_introduction' (issues with created_at >= inflection_date_utc); phases are computed at compute-time by scripts/09_compute_metrics.py reading inflection_date_utc from _metadata.

linear_references_in_repo.pr_template_excerpt_note: Line 5 contains the '## Linear Ticket' section heading; line 7 contains '< Replace with Linear Link ( [create](https://linear.new?title=Awesome-pr-without-linear-ticket) or [search](https://linear.app/rudderstack/search) linear ticket) or  >'. This confirms Linear is the canonical issue tracker for code changes in this repository. The canonical Linear ticket key pattern is [A-Z]{2,}-\d+ (e.g., 'RUD-1234', 'BLZ-5678'); scripts/03_extract_pulls.py extracts this pattern from PR body text to populate the linked_issue_keys field on each PR row.

pr_template_evidence.line_7_summary: links to https://linear.new (issue creation) and https://linear.app/rudderstack/search (issue search)

linear_references_in_repo.issue_template_excerpt_note: The bug-report.md template is a standard GitHub-style bug-report Markdown form (Describe the bug, Steps to reproduce, Expected behavior, Screenshots, Desktop info, Smartphone info, Additional context). It does NOT contain an explicit Linear link, in contrast to .github/pull_request_template.md. The AAP §0.2.1.1 description of this file as 'Documents that the issue tracker is Linear (external)' is partially accurate: the file establishes that bug reports are gathered via GitHub Issues (with no internal pointer to Linear in the template body), while the PR-side template is the file that names Linear explicitly. For Metric 12 (Defects Out of SLA), the canonical defect-tracker source remains Linear (per the PR template); the bug-report.md template provides the inbound GitHub-Issues channel through which external bug reports flow into the repository before being triaged into Linear.
